data.q: Which LINQ operator performs an inner join on two sequences based on matching keys?
data.e: Join performs an inner join. GroupJoin performs a left outer join (grouped). SelectMany flattens sequences. Zip merges sequences by index.

data.q: What is the primary difference between IQueryable<T> and IEnumerable<T> when using LINQ?
o: IQueryable executes in-memory; IEnumerable executes on the database server
IQueryable builds an expression tree for remote execution; IEnumerable uses delegates for in-memory execution
IEnumerable supports deferred execution; IQueryable does not
IQueryable is only for XML data sources
data.e: IQueryable<T> uses Expression<Func<T, bool>> to build expression trees translated by a provider (e.g., EF Core to SQL). IEnumerable<T> uses Func<T, bool> for immediate in-memory filtering.

data.q: Which method allows you to create a custom aggregation using a seed value, an accumulator function, and a result selector?
data.e: Aggregate is the general aggregation operator (fold/reduce). The overload Aggregate<TSource, TAccumulate, TResult>(seed, func, resultSelector) provides full control.

data.q: In LINQ query syntax, what does the 'into' keyword do when used after a 'group by' or 'join' clause?
o: Continues the query with the result of the group/join as a new range variable
Projects the grouped results into an anonymous type
data.e: 'into' creates a temporary identifier for the result of a group or join clause, allowing subsequent query clauses (like select, where, orderby) to operate on that result.

data.q: What is the behavior of the 'DefaultIfEmpty' method when called on an empty sequence?
o: Returns a sequence containing a single element: the default value of the element type (or a specified default)
data.e: DefaultIfEmpty is essential for Left Outer Joins in LINQ. If the source is empty, it yields a sequence with one default(T) element (or a provided default value).

data.q: Which operator is used to perform a 'Left Outer Join' in LINQ method syntax?
o: Join combined with DefaultIfEmpty on the right sequence
GroupJoin combined with SelectMany and DefaultIfEmpty on the right sequence
data.e: LINQ has no 'LeftJoin' operator. A left outer join is achieved by GroupJoin (which groups right elements by left key), then SelectMany over the grouped right sequence with DefaultIfEmpty().

o: Projects each element of a sequence to an IEnumerable<T> and flattens the resulting sequences into one sequence
Selects multiple properties into an anonymous type
Filters a sequence based on multiple predicates
data.e: SelectMany is the bind operation for the List/Sequence monad. It flattens a sequence of sequences (IEnumerable<IEnumerable<T>> -> IEnumerable<T>).

data.q: How does 'AsEnumerable()' affect a LINQ query on an IQueryable source (e.g., Entity Framework)?
o: It forces the query to execute immediately and return a List<T>
It changes the compilation of subsequent operators from Expression Trees to Delegates, forcing client-side evaluation
It enables parallel execution via PLINQ
It caches the query results in memory
data.e: AsEnumerable() casts IQueryable<T> to IEnumerable<T>. Subsequent LINQ operators (Where, Select, etc.) bind to Enumerable extensions (Func delegates) instead of Queryable extensions (Expression trees), pulling data to client before processing.

data.q: What is the result of 'SequenceEqual' when comparing two sequences with the same elements in different orders?
o: True only if a custom IEqualityComparer is provided
data.e: SequenceEqual compares elements pairwise by index. Order matters. To compare unordered sets, use set operators (Intersect/Except) or sort first.

data.q: Which operator returns the single element of a sequence, or a default value if the sequence is empty, but throws if there is more than one element?
data.e: SingleOrDefault returns the only element or default(T). It throws InvalidOperationException if the sequence contains more than one element. FirstOrDefault returns the first regardless of count.

o: The query is executed immediately when defined
The query is executed only when the result is enumerated (e.g., via foreach, ToList())
The query is compiled to SQL but not sent to the server
The query runs on a background thread automatically
data.e: Most LINQ operators use deferred execution (yield return). The query variable stores the query definition, not results. Execution happens on enumeration. Exceptions: ToList, ToArray, Count, First, Single (Immediate Execution).

data.q: Which method optimizes a LINQ to Objects query by using a HashSet internally for lookups?
data.e: While Join uses a HashSet internally, manually converting a lookup source to a HashSet and using Contains inside a Where predicate (or Join) is the standard way to ensure O(1) lookups for 'IN' style filters in LINQ to Objects.

data.q: What does the 'Let' keyword allow in LINQ query syntax?
o: Introduces a new range variable to store the result of a sub-expression
data.e: 'let' allows storing the result of an expression (e.g., a calculated property or sub-query) in a new range variable to avoid recalculating it or to make the query readable.

data.q: How do you perform a 'Group By' on multiple keys in LINQ method syntax?
o: group by new { Key1 = x.Prop1, Key2 = x.Prop2 }
data.e: GroupBy accepts a key selector function. To group by multiple keys, return an anonymous type (or Tuple/ValueTuple) containing all key properties. The compiler handles equality/hashing for anonymous types.

data.q: What is the purpose of the 'AsQueryable()' extension method?
o: Converts an IEnumerable<T> to an IQueryable<T> by wrapping it in an EnumerableQuery provider
Executes the query against a database
data.e: AsQueryable() wraps an in-memory IEnumerable<T> in an IQueryable<T> using EnumerableQuery. This allows in-memory collections to be treated as queryable sources (useful for testing or uniform APIs), but it still executes via LINQ to Objects (delegates), not a remote provider.

data.q: Which operator partitions a sequence into two sequences based on a predicate, returning a Tuple of (matched, notMatched)?
o: None of the above (requires custom implementation or MoreLINQ)
data.e: Standard LINQ does not have a 'Partition' or 'Split' operator that returns a Tuple of two sequences in one pass. GroupBy evaluates the predicate twice (or buffers). MoreLINQ provides 'Partition'.

data.q: In LINQ to Entities (EF Core), why might a query throw 'InvalidOperationException: The LINQ expression could not be translated'?
o: The query uses a C# method or property that has no SQL translation
The query returns too many rows
data.e: EF Core translates Expression Trees to SQL. If the query contains client-side logic (e.g., custom C# methods, ToString() overloads, complex property getters) that the provider cannot translate, it throws this exception. Fix: Use client evaluation (AsEnumerable) or rewrite using translatable constructs.
